from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: The Plane-Cone Intersection", [
            "A double-napped cone is our starting shape.",
            "A plane slices the cone at various angles.",
            "Different angles create circles, ellipses, parabolas, hyperbolas."
        ])
        
        # Animation Objects
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1, height=2, direction=OUT).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.5)
        plane = Polygon(LEFT*2+UP*1, RIGHT*2+UP*1, RIGHT*2+DOWN*1, LEFT*2+DOWN*1).set_fill(GRAY, opacity=0.3)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_in_area(cone, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(cone))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_in_area(plane, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(plane))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Representing an ellipse intersection
        ellipse = Ellipse(width=0.8, height=1.2, color="#FF5733")
        self.place_at_grid(ellipse, 'D5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(ellipse))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Introducing Dandelin Spheres", [
            "Meet the Dandelin Spheres, a geometric bridge.",
            "They fit perfectly inside the cone's interior.",
            "They are tangent to both cone and plane."
        ])
        
        # Create cone and cutting plane visualization
        cone = Cone(base_radius=1.5, height=3, direction=DOWN).set_color(BLUE).set_opacity(0.3)
        plane = Polygon(
            np.array([-1, 0.5, 1]), np.array([1, 0.5, 1]),
            np.array([1, 0.5, -1]), np.array([-1, 0.5, -1])
        ).set_color(YELLOW).set_opacity(0.5).rotate(30*DEGREES, axis=RIGHT)
        
        sphere1 = Sphere(radius=0.4).set_color(RED).set_opacity(0.6)
        sphere2 = Sphere(radius=0.4).set_color(ORANGE).set_opacity(0.6)
        
        tangency1 = Dot(color="#33FF57").scale(0.5)
        tangency2 = Dot(color="#33FF57").scale(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(cone), FadeIn(plane))
        self.place_in_area(sphere1, 'A1', 'C3', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere1))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(RED)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.place_in_area(sphere2, 'D4', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(sphere2))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(ORANGE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            FadeIn(tangency1), 
            FadeIn(tangency2)
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#33FF57")
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Tangency points on the plane become the foci.",
            "Distance sum to foci is constant for ellipses.",
            "This length equals the distance between circles of tangency."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Connecting the Dots: The Ellipse Proof", lecture_lines)
        
        # Ellipse
        ellipse = Ellipse(width=3, height=2, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(ellipse, "B2", "E5")
        
        # Foci
        f1 = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        f2 = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(f1, "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(f2, "C5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        f1_label = Text("F1", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).next_to(f1, UP, buff=0.1)
        f2_label = Text("F2", font_size=20, color=YELLOW).next_to(f2, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        # Point on ellipse
        p = Dot(color=WHITE)
        p.move_to(ellipse.point_from_proportion(0.2))
        
        # Connecting lines
        line1 = Line(p.get_center(), f1.get_center(), color="#33A1FF")
        line2 = Line(p.get_center(), f2.get_center(), color="#33A1FF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(ellipse))
        self.play(FadeIn(f1, f1_label, f2, f2_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#33A1FF"))
        self.play(Create(p))
        self.play(Create(line1), Create(line2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        # Animate point moving
        self.play(
            MoveAlongPath(p, ellipse),
            UpdateFromFunc(line1, lambda l: l.put_start_and_end_on(p.get_center(), f1.get_center())),
            UpdateFromFunc(line2, lambda l: l.put_start_and_end_on(p.get_center(), f2.get_center())),
            run_time=4
        )
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Parabolas and hyperbolas also use this tangency principle.",
            "Shifting the plane morphs the resulting conic section.",
            "Tangency remains the key to all conic behavior."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Generalization and Conclusion", lecture_lines)
        
        # Load Assets
        plane_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/plane.svg").set_color(YELLOW)
        sphere_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/sphere.svg").set_color(BLUE)
        
        # Visualization
        self.place_in_area(plane_icon, "B2", "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_in_area(sphere_icon, "D2", "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Rotate(plane_icon, angle=PI/4, about_point=self.grid["B3"]))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(sphere_icon.animate.shift(RIGHT * 1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(FadeToColor(VGroup(plane_icon, sphere_icon), WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Unveiling the Beauty of Conic Sections: The Dandelin Spheres
outline.target_audience: High school geometry or early university mathematics students

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Plane-Cone Intersection
sections.content: Briefly define a double-napped cone and a cutting plane. Visualize how varying the angle of the plane relative to the cone's axis generates circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas.
sections.example: An animation showing a flat blade slicing through a 3D ice cream cone at different angles to reveal 2D cross-sections.

sections.title: Introducing Dandelin Spheres
sections.content: Introduce the 'Dandelin Spheres' as the geometric bridge. Explain that these are imaginary spheres tucked inside the cone, tangent to both the cone (along a circle) and the cutting plane (at a single point).
sections.example: A 3D model of a transparent cone containing a glowing sphere that perfectly touches the inner surface and the cutting plane at a single point F.

sections.title: Connecting the Dots: The Ellipse Proof
sections.content: Explain that the points of tangency between the spheres and the plane are the 'foci' of the conic section. Show that the sum of distances from any point on the ellipse to the two foci is constant (equal to the distance between the two circles of tangency).
sections.example: Two squirrels at points F1 and F2 (the foci) on the cutting plane, showing that a thread stretched from one to the other via a point on the ellipse remains constant in length.

sections.title: Generalization and Conclusion
sections.content: Extend the logic: explain that for parabolas and hyperbolas, the setup changes slightly (one sphere or different sphere placements), but the tangency principle remains the fundamental 'key' to why these shapes behave the way they do.
sections.example: A fast-paced visual morphing: showing how shifting the plane until it is parallel to the cone's side turns an ellipse into a parabola.
